newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares level off after sharp rise.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares level off after sharp rise.

text.p: 0850 GMT - Italian shares leveled off in mid-morning trading on Monday after roaring ahead at the opening bell in a flurry of buying after Friday's surprise discount rate cut by the Bank of Italy.
* The all-share Mibtel index rose 0.34 percent to 13.433, falling back from a record high of 13,542, while the blue chip Mib30 index was up 0.36 percent at 20,426.

* State-controlled energy group ENI jumped to 9,800 lire in early trading after completion of the third tranche of its public offer on Friday but quickly eased back to 9,760 lire -- an advance of 1.92 percent on the end of last week.

*"The market was up on a wave of enthusiasm over the rate cut but the reduction, when it came, was smaller than what many people had been expecting," said a Milan-based stockbroker. "On the other hand people now think there could still be room for another cut later on," he added.
* Brokers said ENI shares could come off later in the day once investors knew the exact size of their allotments.

* A factor weighing on the market in the medium term is that Italian mutual funds do not expect a next inflow of money for at least two months with the ENI issue and other privatisations private savings.
